fixture.name: messy
fixture.description: Deliberately hostile. Every file breaks the ingest path in a specific documented way. This is the fixture that matters: real personal vaults look like this, not like minimal/.

hostile_cases.breaks: Headings are bold and numerically prefixed (`**1. History**`). Normalising them by stripping only spaces, underscores and hyphens yields `**1.history**`, which matches no alias, and the section is discarded.
No frontmatter at all. Type must come from the folder heuristic. Also carries a callout and an inline hashtag that must survive.
Contains a fenced code block whose body is `---` delimited YAML. Naive frontmatter detection reads the fence as a second frontmatter block and truncates the file.
No gender field. The name carries a strong feminine statistical prior while the title and body are masculine. A model with no correction will produce she/her.
Has a `## Smells Like` section matching no canonical field. Must be retained and retrievable rather than dropped.
Wiki-links to [[The Chancellor]], an entity that has no file. A dangling link must not abort compilation or create a phantom character.
No type, no name, no heading structure, in a folder with no type heuristic. Must not be discarded and must not be misclassified as a character.

entities.name: King Yuna
entities.why_gender: No gender field. Must be inferred from the title 'King' and the body, never from the name.

entities.name: Lord Anneke
entities.why_gender: The critical case. Title and body are unambiguously masculine; the name is not.

must_not_exist.name: The Chancellor
must_not_exist.why: Referenced by a dangling wiki-link only. Compilation must tolerate it without inventing an entity.

ingest_must_retain.why: Body of a bold-numeric heading section. Losing this is Bug 1 recurring.
The goals section, under a heading named 'What He Wants' rather than 'Goals'.
Non-canonical section. Must land in an overflow bucket, not the bin.

ingest_must_retain.substring: loyal to individuals rather than institutions
ingest_must_retain.why: Appears AFTER the code fence. If fence handling is wrong, everything past it is truncated.
Inside a `> [!secret]` callout. Must be ingested, and is the payload for the multi-hop retrieval case below.
Untyped loose note. The data lake principle says this is still retrievable.

edges.why: Explicit wiki-link plus 'Held for the crown by'.
Riots began at the granary there.

retrieval.query: who knows about the hidden causeway
retrieval.why: Payload sits inside a callout block. Fails outright if callouts are dropped at ingest.

retrieval.query: why do people resent the crown
retrieval.why: Thematic, no shared proper noun with the source. Dense embeddings should beat BM25 here; the inverse of the Thornwick case in minimal/.
Rare proper noun, also an alias. BM25 should beat dense here.
Multi-hop. The connection lives only in an untyped scratch note. Hardest case in the set; expected to fail before migration_plan.md 3.4 lands.
Depends on the bold-numeric heading body having survived ingest.

The original reported instance of the bug.
